# Block catalog (generated by inference/blocks/scripts/build-catalog.mjs; do not edit)

51 block(s). Call ListBlocks(category?, query?) for the live list, GetBlock(id) for props, AddBlock(id) to copy one into src/blocks/<id>/.

## transitions

- `flash-cut`: Flash cut. Hard cut hidden behind a quick colour flash; use for beats, impacts and camera-flash moments.
- `glitch-cut`: Glitch cut. Scene change through jittering horizontal slices (slices is clamped to 2-24); use for tech, gaming or error-themed cuts.
- `ink-reveal`: Ink reveal. New scene spreads from a point through an organic wobbling clip-path; use for soft, artistic reveals.
- `whip-blur`: Whip blur. Fast whip pan between scenes with motion blur; use for quick travel or high-energy cuts.
- `wipe-edges`: Wipe edges. Wipe between two scenes with a coloured bar riding the moving edge; use for energetic section changes.
- `wipe-slide`: Wipe slide. Directional wipe from one scene to the next: the arriving scene is revealed by a moving clip-path edge with an ease-in-out curve.
- `zoom-through`: Zoom through. Old scene zooms past the camera while the new one settles in; use to dive into a new topic or detail.

## titles

- `char-stagger`: Character stagger. Letters pop in one by one with a springy overshoot; use for playful or punchy short titles.
- `counter-number`: Counter number. Big number that counts to a target with a label; use for stats, milestones and KPIs.
- `gsap-kinetic-title`: GSAP kinetic title. Title whose characters rise in with a GSAP SplitText timeline. The timeline is built paused and sought from the frame, so every frame is deterministic.
- `kinetic-title`: Kinetic title. Centered title that lands word by word: each word rises and fades in on a spring, staggered by a few frames.
- `lower-third-bar`: Lower third: bar. Solid name bar with an accent stripe in the lower left; use to introduce a speaker or place.
- `lower-third-glass`: Lower third: glass. Frosted translucent name card that floats up in the lower left; use over busy footage or imagery.
- `lower-third-minimal`: Lower third: minimal. Text only over a thin drawn line; use for clean, documentary-style credits.
- `marquee-ticker`: Marquee ticker. Endless scrolling news-style band of text; use for headlines, announcements or promo strips.
- `text-mask-reveal`: Text mask reveal. Huge letters filled with a drifting gradient, wiped in from the left; use for bold opening titles.
- `typewriter-cursor`: Typewriter with cursor. Text types out behind a blinking cursor; use for code, terminals, quotes and reveals of a sentence.
- `word-reveal`: Word reveal. Words rise out of a mask one after another; use for headlines and key statements.

## captions

- `caption-boxed`: Caption boxed. Use for clean, professional captions on a rounded dark panel with the spoken word on an accent chip (explainers, interviews). The `captions` prop is a @remotion/captions Caption[].
- `caption-karaoke`: Caption karaoke. Use for word-by-word spoken captions where each word fills with colour as it is said (talking heads, voice-overs). The `captions` prop is a @remotion/captions Caption[].
- `caption-outline-bold`: Caption outline bold. Use for bold upper-case captions with a thick outline that stay readable over busy footage; the spoken word changes colour. The `captions` prop is a @remotion/captions Caption[].
- `caption-pop-word`: Caption pop word. Use for punchy short-form captions that show one big word at a time, popping in as it is spoken. The `captions` prop is a @remotion/captions Caption[].

## charts

- `chart-bars`: Bar chart. Use to compare a handful of categories: horizontal bars grow in one after another with value labels. Transparent overlay with light text by default (theme 'dark'): put it on a dark backdrop, or pass theme="light" for light backdrops.
- `chart-donut`: Donut chart. Use to show parts of a whole (shares, budget split): a donut that sweeps open with a total and a legend. Transparent overlay with light text by default (theme 'dark'): put it on a dark backdrop, or pass theme="light" for light backdrops.
- `chart-line-draw`: Line chart draw-on. Use to show a trend over time: a smooth line with area fill that draws itself left to right. Transparent overlay with light text by default (theme 'dark'): put it on a dark backdrop, or pass theme="light" for light backdrops.
- `kpi-ticker`: KPI ticker. Use to land one headline number: a big figure that counts up with a label and an optional change chip. The figure size fits the frame width (9:16 safe); override with fontSize.
- `progress-ring`: Progress ring. Use to show completion or a score out of 100: a ring that fills while the percentage counts up.
- `sparkline`: Sparkline card. Use for a small trend callout next to a metric: a compact card with the latest value and a self-drawing line.

## maps

- `map-pin-pulse`: Map pin pulse. Use to mark places on a world map: pins drop in and send out pulsing rings with city labels (offline).
- `map-region-highlight`: Map region highlight. Use to call out a country by ISO code on a world map: it lights up and the camera eases toward it (offline). The label sits on the country.
- `map-route-arc`: Map route arc. Use to show a journey or shipment between two cities: a great-circle route draws on with a travelling dot (offline).

## effects

- `bokeh`: Bokeh. Floating soft light circles for a dreamy depth-of-field feel over a scene.
- `confetti`: Confetti. Seeded confetti burst for celebrations and milestones.
- `crt-scanlines`: CRT scanlines. Wrap a scene in an old CRT monitor look: scanlines, rounded screen, vignette and flicker. Use for retro or gaming moments.
- `film-grain`: Film grain. Overlay animated film grain on any scene for a filmic, analogue texture.
- `halftone`: Halftone. Use for a comic or print halftone dot look over a scene, strongest at the edges (stylised intros, comic-book beats). Render cost: masks and rotates a full-frame layer, about +0.36 s/frame at 1080p (roughly 5 minutes extra for a 30 s film), so apply it to short beats, not whole films.
- `light-leak`: Light leak. Warm drifting light leaks blended over a scene for a nostalgic film feel, good for transitions and intros.
- `vhs-glitch`: VHS glitch. Glitch a scene with RGB channel split and horizontal tear bands in seeded bursts. Use for tension cuts or retro intros.
- `vignette`: Vignette. Darken or tint the edges to focus attention on the centre of a scene.

## backgrounds

- `aurora`: Aurora. Soft waving aurora bands over a night sky; calm, premium background.
- `gradient-mesh`: Gradient mesh. Modern slowly drifting multi-colour gradient background; use behind titles and UI.
- `particle-field`: Particle field. Seeded drifting dots with optional connecting lines; use for tech, network and data themes.
- `perspective-grid`: Perspective grid. Retro synthwave 3D grid floor scrolling toward the viewer; use for tech, gaming and 80s themes.

## devices

- `browser-frame`: Browser frame. Put screenshots or UI inside a browser window with chrome; use for web product demos.
- `cursor-click`: Cursor click. Animated mouse cursor that glides to a point and clicks with a ripple; use to guide attention in UI demos.
- `laptop-frame`: Laptop frame. Put a desktop UI inside a laptop with base; use for SaaS and software showcases.
- `phone-frame`: Phone frame. Put app screens or vertical video inside a smartphone bezel; use for mobile demos.
- `toast-notification`: Toast notification. Notification card that slides in, holds and slides out; use for success messages and alerts in UI scenes.

## shapes

- `arrow-draw`: Arrow draw. Hand-drawn style arrow that draws itself along given points; use to point at something on screen.
- `callout-bubble`: Callout bubble. Speech or annotation bubble with a pointer that pops in; use to label or comment on part of the frame.
- `check-draw`: Check draw. Animated checkmark inside a circle that draws itself; use for success, done and completed states.
